# Field Function and Value Modifications

Also called: Scalar Field Modification, Field Function Modification

## Overview
This family of methods modifies the scalar field function $f(x,y,z)$ or its evaluation logic prior to or during the Marching Cubes traversal, rather than altering the mesh topology or lookup tables directly. By changing the input values, these techniques enable specific geometric behaviors such as preserving sharp features, enabling interactive terrain editing, or resolving topological ambiguities through bilinear assumptions. They differ from sibling methods like [Snap Marching Cubes](2181-snap-marching-cubes.md) (which snaps vertices to grid lines) or [Edge Groups](14157-edge-groups.md) (which groups edges for simplification) by operating on the data domain rather than the geometric output domain.

## Shared principles
All variants in this family accept a 3D scalar field defined on a structured grid and produce a triangle mesh. They share the foundational mechanism of determining edge intersections via a case index derived from vertex signs relative to an isovalue, as described in [Marching Cubes Lookup and Configuration](2518-marching-cubes-lookup-and-configuration.md). However, they diverge in how the scalar value at a query point $(x,y,z)$ is computed. Instead of a direct lookup or simple linear interpolation of grid values, the field function is augmented. This augmentation may involve:
1.  **Feature Detection Logic**: Computing gradients and comparing normal angles to inject new vertices (Extended EMC).
2.  **Additive Superposition**: Summing base procedural noise with user-defined analytic functions (Additive Metaball).
3.  **Bilinear Assumptions**: Using face-wise bilinear interpolation coefficients to resolve connectivity in ambiguous cases (Enhanced EMC).

## Subtopics

### [Extended Marching Cubes](1630-extended-marching-cubes.md)
Enhances standard MC by preserving sharp geometric features. It detects sharp angles between surface normals at edge intersections and uses Quadratic Error Functions (QEFs) to place new vertices at feature locations, forming triangle fans. Choose this when sharp edges/corners must be preserved without smoothing.

### [Additive Metaball Modification for Marching Cubes](16595-additive-metaball-modification-for-marching-cubes.md)
Enables dynamic, local terrain editing (digging/placing) by superimposing user-defined metaball density functions onto a base noise field. It avoids global artifacts by not altering the base noise sequence. Choose this for interactive voxel-based editing where the base terrain must remain stable.

### [Enhanced Marching Cubes](22926-enhanced-marching-cubes.md)
Modifies the lookup logic to resolve topological ambiguities and cover large holes by replacing linear edge interpolation with midpoint selection and applying 20 new rules based on bilinear interpolation conditions. Choose this when standard MC produces holes or incorrect topology in curved surfaces.

## Background
The concept of modifying field functions to improve surface extraction quality emerged as standard linear interpolation in Marching Cubes was found to smooth out sharp features and fail on ambiguous topological cases. Extended Marching Cubes introduced QEF-based feature preservation to address the smoothing issue . Additive Metaball methods were developed to support interactive editing in voxel games without regenerating global noise . Enhanced Marching Cubes addressed the ambiguity problem by introducing bilinear interpolation assumptions on cube faces to determine connectivity, expanding the rule set from 15 to 35 .
